text_summary.body: Tattenai acted on Darius's decree; the elders built and prospered through Haggai and Zechariah, and finished the house by the command of God and the decree of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, on 3 Adar of Darius's sixth year; the exiles dedicated it with 100 bulls, 200 rams, 400 lambs and 12 male goats for the tribes of Israel, and set the priests and Levites in their divisions.

setting.body: On Babylonian Nisan reckoning Darius's sixth year ran from spring 516 to spring 515, placing 3 Adar in late February or March 515.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V10B5RPQCMG56ABNE83R1V
constraints.textual_assertion: This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king
assumptions: Babylonian Nisan-based years: year 6 = spring 516 – spring 515, so Adar falls in Feb–Mar 515 (Parker & Dubberstein table).

terminology.gloss: A later king named alongside Cyrus and Darius; Kidner (via Guzik) and Batten treat it as completing the picture or as a gloss.

competing_reconstructions.label: Spring 515 BC
competing_reconstructions.summary: Adar of year 6 of Darius I.

competing_reconstructions.label: Interval from 587/586: about 70 years
proponents: Temple-desolation reading of Jeremiah's seventy years

competing_reconstructions.label: Third or twenty-third of Adar; sixth or ninth year
competing_reconstructions.summary: Keil explains the 1 Esdras reading as an adjustment to give an eight-day dedication ending the year.

not_applicable.commentary: Enduring Word on Ezra/Nehemiah was not consulted in this Daniel session; Guzik's dates are recorded on the seventy-weeks prophecy.
